One row per item (an item carried by several pages is one row; extra carriers in col 10). Built on Nov 23, 2026 from: every saved page whose address is a central state or Party outlet (a scan of the saved pages' addresses), the rows of the project's earlier searches, those searches' notes of what they had not reached, and further searches made for this table. Scope: central Party and state media (People's Daily group incl. Overseas Edition, People.cn, Global Times/Huanqiu, China Economic Weekly, the Party members' paper; Xinhua group incl. Economic Information Daily, Reference News, Xinhua Finance; China Media Group incl. CCTV, CGTN, Yuyuan Tantian; Guangming Daily group incl. Zhonghua Dushubao; Economic Daily; China Daily; Qiushi; Study Times; Science and Technology Daily) and one city Party paper (Beijing Daily). Commercial outlets (The Paper, Sina, IT Home, Eastmoney, Tencent News) appear only as carriers. Columns: 1 date = the page's own publication date (Beijing time) | 2 outlet = who published the words | 3 kind = signed commentary | unsigned commentary | news | interview | social post | official text carried | analysis | notice | 4 stance toward buying Nvidia chips = warns (discourages buying or using) | welcomes (favours imports or Nvidia's presence) | mixed (both in one item) | neutral (reports without advice) | self-reliance (stresses home-made chips without advice on buying) | other | 5 speaker = whose words the key sentence is | 6 key sentence = exact words from the saved page (checked against the saved copy by script) | 7 saved id of the page that carries the key sentence | 8 held = saved and read | found = known, not saved | 9 original? = original outlet page | outlet's own channel on a platform | relay (another site) | 10 other carriers (saved ids) | 11 the row's place in the list of the earlier search it came from, as list:line (- where it was found another way) | 12 note | 13 subject = chips for AI computing (the item is about Nvidia's chips for data centres and AI and China: their sale, American curbs or approvals, their security, Chinese buyers, Chinese alternatives) | a product with an Nvidia chip (a car, robot, computer or other product or service of a Chinese firm that uses an Nvidia chip or platform, with nothing on the chips for AI computing) | Nvidia as a company (its shares, results, rankings, its chief executive's visits or remarks, with nothing on chips for China) | other (an item on another matter that names Nvidia or its chips in passing)

# Added Nov 24, 2026: rows 43 to 75, found by a second search for this table, by web searches with other words, the outlets' list pages and links on saved pages, and title-word scans of the e-papers of People's Daily, its Overseas Edition, Guangming Daily and Economic Daily; for Jul 31 to Sept 24, 2025 a second search of those weeks, and after Sept 24, 2025 a sample from searches and links, not a census of those papers (the note of each row says how it was found). Rows 30 and 42 replaced and rows 15, 17 and 34 annotated the same day. Stance rule applied to rows 43 to 75 and checked against rows 1 to 42: warns = the item, in its own words or a speaker's it quotes, says Nvidia's chips carry security risks, or that Nvidia must prove them safe, or argues against buying or using them; mixed = that, together with words that Nvidia or American chipmakers are welcome or that imports may resume; a sentence that only reports or predicts buyers' reluctance is not a warning. Rows 49, 52 and 64 are coded otherwise than the second search coded them, as each row's note says. A baseline for Jan 2024 to Jun 2025, in these columns and by this rule but gathered later by other routes (web searches, the Yuyuan Tantian index on CCTV's site, a title-word scan of four papers) and not a census, is kept apart in tables/state_media_baseline_2024_2025h1.tsv (174 items since Nov 26, 2026, 1 of which warns; 49 items until then); its rows are not counted here. Rows 9, 10, 11, 27, 37, 48, 54, 55, 67 and 74 were recoded on Nov 25, 2026 after two blind second coders and a third reader; an item that carries the regulator's own words on the chips' security or its demand for proof counts as warning, as row 13 counts for the commentary it carries.

# Changed Nov 26, 2026. (a) Rows 75 to 297 added: every saved page of an outlet in scope that names Nvidia or its chips and was not yet a row or a row's carrier (489 pages), coded by this table's rule five times independently (two readers of every page and three further codings), a majority deciding each cell and 23 pages ruled singly; pages that carry the same item joined into one row, and pages that carry an item the table already held named in column 10 of that item's row (34 pages on 12 rows). These rows were found by a scan of the saved pages, not by a search list (column 11: -); what the saved pages hold after Sept 24, 2025 is far more than before and is still not a full count of what these outlets printed. (b) One row taken out: the notice of Apr 24, 2026 of China Media Group (a list of works entered for a journalism award): its page does not name Nvidia. THE ROW NUMBERS IN THE TWO LINES ABOVE are those of the table before this: a number above 34 there is one lower now. (c) Column 13, subject, added for every row: two readings of each page, a third where they differed. Items on a product with an Nvidia chip stay in the table; a count of items about the chips for AI computing takes the rows of that subject. (d) Counts as the table stands: 297 items; 34 warn, 23 of them dated Jul 31 to Sept 24, 2025 and 11 outside those weeks (6 of these from Dec 9, 2025 to Jan 14, 2026). (e) Joined later on Nov 26, 2026: 13 rows of (a) proved to be the same piece as another row on a second site (a dispatch or article carried by another outlet's site, some dated a day later); two independent readers read each pair of pages, with pairs known to be the same and known to differ among them. Each such page is now named in column 10 of its item's row (12 rows), and the table has 13 rows fewer than (a) first added; none of the 13 was a warning. One pair with the same text under two outlets' own credits stays as two rows.
